Phobos.VehicleSystems.PhobosCouplingDef.label: drawbar and pin
Phobos.VehicleSystems.PhobosCouplingDef.description: A flat bar at the back of a tractor. The trailer's eye or clevis is pinned to it. Most towed farm implements couple this way.

Phobos.VehicleSystems.PhobosCouplingDef.label: pintle hook
Phobos.VehicleSystems.PhobosCouplingDef.description: A hook with a latch, taking a round ring on the trailer's drawbar. Heavy carts and trucks use it, as the ring swivels in the hook on rough ground.

Phobos.VehicleSystems.PhobosCouplingDef.label: pick-up hitch
Phobos.VehicleSystems.PhobosCouplingDef.description: A hook that lifts into the trailer's ring, so the driver can couple from the seat. Common on grain and silage trailers.

Phobos.VehicleSystems.PhobosCouplingDef.label: ball hitch
Phobos.VehicleSystems.PhobosCouplingDef.description: A ball on the towing vehicle and a cup on the trailer. For light trailers.

Phobos.VehicleSystems.PhobosCouplingDef.label: heavy ball hitch
Phobos.VehicleSystems.PhobosCouplingDef.description: A large ball for heavy farm trailers, held down by a clamp.

Phobos.VehicleSystems.PhobosCouplingDef.label: three-point linkage
Phobos.VehicleSystems.PhobosCouplingDef.description: Two lower arms and a top link that carry an implement and lift it, rather than tow it. Mounted ploughs, cultivators and sprayers hang from it.

Phobos.VehicleSystems.PhobosCouplingDef.label: articulation pivot
Phobos.VehicleSystems.PhobosCouplingDef.description: The heavy hinge between the two halves of an articulated vehicle, which bends it to steer. It is part of the vehicle and is never uncoupled.
